nodes.label: The Phosphor Archive (Creative North Star)
nodes.rationale: The glow is the light source, not decoration; green is the archive's default voice while amber stays the rare earnest/safety/selection channel so its rarity keeps meaning 'pay attention'. The system explicitly rejects corporate/Google-Maps neutrality, Strava/Instagram social polish, cutesy gamification, and the generic 'modern dark-mode SaaS' look named as anti-references in PRODUCT.md — dark is not the same as this; retro-computing intent is the difference.

nodes.label: The Two-Phosphor Rule
nodes.rationale: Only green and amber are voices; green is the default and amber is earnest/selected. Everything else (surfaces, lines) is a near-black tint of green, and any third decorative color is forbidden — this keeps the system reading as a CRT terminal rather than a generic dark theme.

nodes.label: The No-White Rule
nodes.rationale: #ffffff and near-white grays are banned on every surface, the basemap included now that the site draws it: white is the failure signature. Every empty/loading/error state falls back to 'surface', and map chrome that arrives white by default (MapLibre's popup box, its tip, the attribution control) is repainted in the palette rather than left as shipped. The rule now has no map-tile carve-out.

nodes.label: The Rarity Rule
nodes.rationale: Amber covers <=10% of any screen. If a screen has amber in more than one role at once, cut it back to the single most-earnest one — this is what keeps amber legible as 'pay attention' rather than becoming a second decorative color.

nodes.label: The One-Grid Rule
nodes.rationale: Everything is monospace (IBM Plex Mono). No proportional font enters the interface, not for 'friendly' body copy and not for headings — the character grid is the brand.

nodes.label: The Restrained-Caps Rule
nodes.rationale: UPPERCASE + tracking is reserved for labels and terminal system-copy only, never body prose, because long uppercase runs kill legibility in the sunlight/outdoor read the product prioritizes.

nodes.label: The Glow-Is-The-Shadow Rule
nodes.rationale: Never add a dark/gray box-shadow or filter: drop-shadow(black). Elevation is always a colored bloom of phosphor (green, or amber for the care channel) — if a component needs to feel raised, raise its glow, not a gray shadow.

nodes.label: The Bloom-Budget Rule
nodes.rationale: Glow must not smear legibility: resting text glow stays <=6px radius so letters keep clean edges in sunlight, and only non-text chrome (frames, active tabs) uses the wide 24-30px halos.

nodes.label: Directions Link Mechanism
nodes.rationale: A Google Maps URL (maps/dir/?api=1&destination=<lat>,<lng>) opened in a new browsing context (target="_blank", rel="noopener noreferrer") is kept as the destination because it is the only single URL that reaches a native maps app on both phone platforms and still degrades to a usable route rather than nothing: a geo: URI is app-neutral and Android honours it, but iOS registers no handler so it is a dead tap in Safari, and maps.apple.com deep-links on Apple's platforms alone. Opening in its own tab leaves the archive tab standing — the map, the selected pin and the open popup are still there to come back to — so the archive is never replaced by a hosted map.

nodes.label: Google My Maps Embed (temporary anachronism)
nodes.rationale: Cities still waiting on the MapLibre migration show the embedded Google My Maps instead — treated as the temporary anachronism the terminal wraps around: framed in a glowing green border, sitting on a dark surface, never allowed to flash raw white.

nodes.label: Task 2: Spot Data on the Real Map
nodes.rationale: Checks that Vienna's 12 real spots read as spread across the city, the 4 demolished spots read as visibly ghosted against the 8 active ones without opening a popup, and re-encoded (-q 72, 1400px long edge) spot photos survive on a real screen.
nodes.norm_label: task 2: spot data on the real map

nodes.label: Task 4: Photo Gallery Rendering
nodes.rationale: Checks the photo gallery's object-fit cropping, focus ring visibility, 44px thumb-tappable arrows, tap/swipe advance smoothness, no white flash while loading on a throttled connection, a legible counter over varied photos, and reduced-motion compliance.

nodes.label: Task 5: Container / Renderer Split
nodes.rationale: A behavior-preserving refactor moved the Google embed into its own component while the container kept the state machine; the checklist items here are regression checks expecting outcomes identical to before the refactor, plus one genuinely new item covering the WebGL-unsupported failure surface once Task 10 gave it something to trigger.

nodes.label: Task 6: Terminal Basemap Style
nodes.rationale: The basemap style module was authored as data before being rendered; walkthrough items check the phosphor wireframe reads correctly at real zoom levels, labels load without collisions, road widths interpolate sensibly across zoom, and no white surface appears while tiles load or fail.

nodes.label: Task 7: Real Map Factory Registered
nodes.rationale: The karma suite can only assert a MAP_FACTORY provider exists in appConfig; whether the lazy maplibre-gl import actually resolves at runtime and renders a Map instance rather than falling through to the failure surface is a browser fact, unverified until walked.

nodes.label: Task 8: The Spot Map Itself
nodes.rationale: SpotMapComponent's spec suite runs entirely against an injected fake map, so gesture behavior (the two-finger pinch-zoom bug the whole pilot exists to fix), camera framing, attribution legibility, pin glow/hit-target sizing, and the no-white guarantee across load/fail/city-switch are all unverified until walked on a real device.

nodes.label: Task 9: The Spot Popup and Pin Selection
nodes.rationale: SpotPopupComponent and the tap-to-select path in SpotMapComponent are covered only by specs run against a fake map and a fake popup. Real-device items cover popup framing with nothing white anywhere, the amber selection ring which rides on MapLibre promoting each spot's string id into feature-state (only a real map exercises this), gallery swipe inside a touch-action:none canvas host, the geo: URI resolving only on a real device, and the fatal/non-fatal error discriminator reading the error payload rather than map.isStyleLoaded().
nodes.norm_label: task 9: the spot popup and pin selection

nodes.label: Task 10: Turn Vienna On
nodes.rationale: config.ts sets Vienna's renderer to MapRendererEnum.MapLibre and the container's @switch renders app-spot-map, as of commit 01797e6 — the change that opens the gate on every other task's on-device items, none of which a headless spec can see.

nodes.label: Task 11: Map Surface Matches Its Documentation
nodes.rationale: Touched only PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md (commit 016d6a7), so nothing became newly reachable, only newly described. DESIGN.md's new 'Map Surface (signature — Vienna)' section was written from the style definition, component templates and stylesheets rather than a running map, so it needs a human look; the task also removed the No-White Rule's map-tile carve-out, prompting a fresh white sweep.
nodes.norm_label: task 11: map surface matches its documentation

nodes.label: Branch Review Fixes (Round 1)
nodes.rationale: Nine post-review fixes; the worker-loading fix is load-bearing because before it the map never finished loading under either a built or dev-served app on a real device, making every other rendered item in every earlier section unreachable until confirmed fixed.

nodes.label: Branch Review Fixes (Round 2)
nodes.rationale: A second review round re-checked round 1's fixes and found more: the directions link needed to leave the archive standing rather than replacing it, tunnels of every class needed removing from the basemap while elevated transit came back, and the no-renderer message needed rewriting for readers who do not know what WebGL is.

nodes.label: Worker Guard Fix (maplibre-gl-worker 404)
nodes.rationale: Before this fix the maplibre-gl worker module 404'd under both ng serve and the production build, so the map never finished loading on a real device; the fix stops the build's worker guard from vouching for a chunk it never actually verified is emitted and delivered under the /spotmap-website/ base path.

nodes.label: WebGL 2 vs WebGL Distinction (No-Renderer Message)
nodes.rationale: The no-renderer failure line now reads '> NO RENDERER // THIS BROWSER CANNOT DRAW THE MAP' — 48 characters against the 31 of '> SIGNAL LOST // MAP UNREACHABLE', the longest phosphor message the failure surfaces carry — and it must still appear immediately with no retry, since rebuilding the map cannot help. It replaces an earlier line that named the browser as too old. The component's own inline comment still frames the trigger narrowly as 'a browser without WebGL 2, not a browser without WebGL at all' (true for an iOS 14 Safari on this path, which has WebGL 1, so 'no WebGL' would be false for it); DESIGN.md's newer rationale broadens that reasoning to any of several causes the app cannot distinguish between, which is why the message now names the outcome instead of a cause.

nodes.label: geo: URI Platform Limitation
nodes.rationale: The geo: URI only resolves on a real device — a desktop browser proves nothing here — and the previous geo: link did nothing on iOS, so directions verification must target iOS Safari specifically as well as Android Chrome, checking the destination label carries the spot's name and that the archive tab (map, popup, selection ring) is still there afterward.
